notes.summary: Reconstructed ordinary CLD multiplier and support lemmas with exact complementary degrees and localized positive coefficient-measure bounds. No universal Bedford–Taylor conclusion is inferred.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks complete immediate statements and proofs in the retained full CLDv2 source, then reconstructs localized middle-positive test decomposition, the weighted ordinary-product estimate, smooth harmonic multiplication, and localization of a possible defect to an explicitly closed locus. Retains both valuation regimes, singularities, nilpotents and original integration weights.
notes.text:
Work on an ordinary open N in the original good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic space, over any complete non-Archimedean field. Let T be positive and d'- and d''-closed of bidegree (p,p), 0<=p<=n-1. Put D=d'd'', q=n-p and r=q-1. Tests for T have degree (q,q); tests for D(hT) have degree (r,r).

The published input is Chambert-Loir–Ducros, arXiv:1204.6277v2, cover dated 25 July 2025; the retained internal title is dated 29 July 2025. Complete immediate statements/proofs and surrounding definitions were checked in the bound full source. CLD 11.1.7 and 15.7.1–2 provide ordinary analytic domains and canonical level-n calculus without nontrivial-valuation or reducedness restrictions. CLD 15.2.2–9 supplies local differential separation, compact smooth cutoffs, scalar density and compact localization. CLD 6.5.2 decomposes symmetric compact diagonal tests into middle-positive compact tests; its analytic support hypothesis holds on good domains. CLD 7.1.1–9 supplies complementary-test currents, smooth products, restriction, the ordinary sheaf property and support. CLD 7.2.8 and 7.2.11–12 supplies positive coefficient Radon measures and ordinary multiplication by locally bounded Borel functions. CLD 7.7.1–8 gives differential duality, locality and DJ=JD. Smooth signs are checked from 1.3.6 and 3.3.10–11. Recursive published foundations are disclosed rather than claimed newly proved.

Localized decomposition: if a symmetric compact (q,q)-test beta has support in an ordinary O subset N, apply CLD 6.5.2 on O and extend the compact outputs by zero to N. This gives beta=eta_+-eta_-, with middle-positive compact eta_+,eta_- supported in O. The extension is smooth because each compact support is closed in the Hausdorff N and contained in O. Output support need not equal beta's support.

Weighted ordinary-product bound: put eta=eta_++eta_-. For every continuous real b,
|<bT,beta>| <= integral |b| d mu_(T,eta) <= sup_(supp eta)|b| <T,eta>.
The coefficient measures for eta_+ and eta_- are positive and compact. Uniqueness and smooth scalar density identify their sum with the coefficient measure for eta. The ordinary product pairs b by the difference of their integrals; the triangle inequality gives the first estimate. Each measure has mass <T,eta_+> or <T,eta_->, by testing a smooth cutoff equal to one on its support. This proves the second estimate with the original middle cone.

Smooth multiplier identity: for ordinary smooth g, D(gT)=T wedge Dg. To prove it, test against a symmetric compact (r,r)-form alpha and set A=g d''alpha-d''g wedge alpha. Leibniz gives
Dg wedge alpha-g Dalpha=-d'A+C,
where C=d'g wedge d''alpha+d''g wedge d'alpha. The J identities give JC=-C, so symmetry of T annihilates C. Closedness annihilates d'A. Consequently <T,Dg wedge alpha>=<T,g Dalpha>; differential duality and smooth multiplication prove the identity. Both closedness equations remain hypotheses. The proof uses correct complementary degrees and does not apply the inconsistent bidegree/bidimension indexing of the printed CLD 8.5.3 statement.

Defect support: suppose Z is ordinary closed and continuous h is ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian on N minus Z. Then R=D(hT) vanishes there by the smooth multiplier identity and restriction, so supp R is contained in Z. It is symmetric because hT is symmetric and DJ=JD. If chi is smooth and equals one near Z intersect supp alpha, then <R,alpha>=<R,chi alpha>: the compact test (1-chi)alpha has support disjoint from Z. No order-zero assertion about R is needed.

The checked analytic support input is precisely CLD 15.2.1: the support of a type (a,b) G-form lies in {x:d_K(x)>=max(a,b)}; it does not meet a closed analytic locus Y in an analytic domain when dim Y<max(a,b). Ordinary smooth forms are G-forms. Its proof combines tropical chart dimension with 3.3.6, then d_K(y)<=dim Y. Here d_K is residual transcendence degree plus rational value-group rank. This is analytic dimension, not a coarse skeleton dimension. CLD 7.3.1 and 7.7.4 also give positivity and double closedness of the original canonical integration current.

No reduction, normalization, scalar extension or tropical pushforward is performed. Actual generic Artinian integration lengths are retained. No previous manuscript result or correctness grant is a premise.

Complete proofs are in sections/01-calculus.md, whole-proof.md and P21.3-paper.tex. whole-source-application-ledger.json contains exact versions, primary paths, literal complete immediate units, hypotheses and application checks. Full primary inputs are retained locally as inputs/cld-v2-full-LOCALONLY.txt and inputs/CLD-v2-LOCALONLY.pdf. Rerun: python reproduce.py. Artifact checks do not establish mathematical correctness.

notes.summary: Proves a direct cutoff removability bound for arbitrary positive doubly closed ordinary currents under off-locus smooth harmonicity. Vanishing weighted errors imply independence; a nonzero detector with smooth trace forces inverse-oscillation cutoff-mass blowup.
notes.detailedSummary: For actual compact detecting tests and cutoffs on one fixed ordinary open, proves |<D(hT),alpha>|<=integral|h-g|dmu_(T,eta). Defines a finite, test-dependent cutoff mass infimum and proves a smooth-trace removability criterion and quantitative obstruction bound. Neither suitable off-locus regularity nor vanishing cutoff errors is established for arbitrary original pairs.
notes.text:
Use n1's original ambient domain and arbitrary positive doubly closed T, with q=n-p and r=q-1. Assume Z subset N is ordinary closed, and h is continuous on N and ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian on N minus Z. Fix a symmetric compact ordinary smooth (r,r)-test alpha and set S=Z intersect supp alpha.

For any ordinary neighborhood O of the compact S, choose an actual compact ordinary smooth chi supported in O, with 0<=chi<=1 and chi=1 near S. Such cutoffs exist by n1; smooth composition enforces the range bound. The symmetric compact form D(chi alpha) has degree (q,q), so n1 gives an actual decomposition
D(chi alpha)=eta_+-eta_-,
where eta_+,eta_- are compact middle-positive forms supported in O. Put eta=eta_++eta_-. For any ordinary smooth zero-Hessian g on the same fixed N,
|<D(hT),alpha>| <= integral_N |h-g| d mu_(T,eta) <= sup_(supp eta)|h-g| <T,eta>.

Complete proof: n1 gives supp R subset Z for R=D(hT), hence <R,alpha>=<R,chi alpha>. Differential duality gives <R,chi alpha>=<hT,D(chi alpha)>. The smooth multiplier identity gives <gT,D(chi alpha)>=<D(gT),chi alpha>=0. Thus the detecting pairing equals <(h-g)T,D(chi alpha)>. Apply n1's weighted ordinary-product estimate. All forms, products and detecting tests are upstairs on the original analytic domain. No nonsmooth wedge, current exhaustion or coarse tropical equality is substituted.

Therefore D(hT)=0 if, for every detecting alpha, a sequence or net of these actual triples on the fixed N has integral |h-g_j| d mu_(T,eta_j) tending to zero. The stronger condition sup_(supp eta_j)|h-g_j| times <T,eta_j> tending to zero suffices. Indeed the displayed inequality bounds a fixed left side by quantities tending to zero; symmetric tests detect the symmetric defect. The functions g_j need not approximate h away from the cutoff supports. Existence of these vanishing triples is an extra hypothesis, not a consequence proved here of D[h]=0.

Define C_(T,alpha)(S;O) to be the infimum of <T,eta_++eta_-> over exactly these cutoffs and positive decompositions supported in O. It is finite and nonnegative for every O: a competitor exists, and every compact smooth test has a finite current value. It is zero when S is empty. It is nondecreasing as O shrinks, because the competitor set decreases. Pointwise finiteness does not imply a uniform bound on shrinking neighborhoods.

Fix smooth zero-Hessian g and a relatively compact ordinary neighborhood O of S. Let omega_g(O)=sup_O |h-g|, finite by continuity. Taking the infimum in the preceding inequality gives
|<D(hT),alpha>| <= omega_g(O) C_(T,alpha)(S;O),
without assuming attainment of the infimum. Thus neighborhoods O_j with omega_g(O_j) C_(T,alpha)(S;O_j) tending to zero force the detecting pairing to vanish.

If h=g on S, arbitrarily small-oscillation neighborhoods exist: intersect a relatively compact neighborhood of S with {|h-g|<epsilon}. A uniformly bounded family of cutoff masses is sufficient for vanishing. Constants are valid reference functions, so locally constant traces are included. Local smooth harmonic trace extensions also work after ordinary localization.

Conversely, if a detecting pairing has absolute value d>0, every such O with omega_g(O)>0 satisfies
C_(T,alpha)(S;O)>=d/omega_g(O).
An O with omega_g(O)=0 is impossible for a nonzero detector. Therefore, when h=g on S, every sequence of small-oscillation neighborhoods forces the cutoff masses to infinity in the presence of a nonzero detecting pairing. This concerns derivative-weighted cutoff mass; it does not assert an atom of T on Z and does not construct a counterexample.

If the hypotheses and vanishing estimates hold on an ordinary cover of a specified W, restriction and the current sheaf property give D(hT)=0 on W. Only established identities for the original current are glued. The cover is not promoted to a basis or to an every-open statement.

The argument applies in every allowed degree, including scalar detecting tests when p=n-1, over both valuation regimes and on the original possibly nonreduced space. Its off-locus regularity and vanishing cutoff conditions remain unproved for arbitrary original pairs and currents.

Full statements and proofs are in sections/02-removability.md, P21.3-paper.tex and whole-proof.md. Rerun: python reproduce.py. These are draft mathematical proofs; successful artifact checks are not a correctness verdict.

notes.summary: Proves analytic-locus removability when dim Z<n-p-1 and h is ordinary smooth zero-Hessian off Z. The top allowed degree excludes no nonempty locus, and the full original P21.3 remains unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Establishes an analytic partial theorem for arbitrary allowed currents, both valuations and nonreduced spaces using defect support and CLD test-support vanishing. Identifies a necessary defect location and the dimensional window where canonical nullity follows but this method does not prove multiplier independence. No universal regularity/cutoff estimate or admissible analytic counterexample is produced; candidate=false.
notes.text:
Let W be a specified ordinary open in the unchanged original ambient X, let 0<=p<=n-1, and put r=n-p-1. Suppose Z subset W is ordinary closed and locally a closed analytic locus of dimension strictly less than r. Suppose h is continuous on W and ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian on W minus Z. Then D(hT)=0 for every positive doubly closed ordinary (p,p)-current T on W. In particular the required Bedford–Taylor equality holds for separately admissible finite continuous psh U,V whose difference satisfies these extra conditions.

Complete proof: n1 gives supp D(hT) subset Z. On each ordinary neighborhood carrying the analytic-locus bound, CLD 15.2.1(b), stated and checked in n1, says that every compact smooth (r,r) detecting test has support disjoint from Z. It therefore pairs to zero with the defect. All complementary tests vanish, so the current is zero on that neighborhood. Ordinary sheaf localization proves zero on W. The same proof works for arbitrary ordinary closed Z under the explicit pointwise condition d_K(z)<r, using 15.2.1(a). No analytic dimension is assigned to an arbitrary skeleton or closed set.

For a locus of pure analytic codimension c, the sufficient integer bound is c>=p+2. For n=2, p=0 allows zero-dimensional analytic loci, while p=1 allows no nonempty locus. For n=3, the upper dimension bounds are one, zero and no nonempty locus. In every dimension, p=n-1 gives r=0 and hence no nonempty-locus conclusion. This is an arbitrary-current partial theorem, not a universal solution.

A necessary location statement also follows, now assuming off-locus smooth zero-Hessian regularity without imposing that dimension inequality. If D(hT) is nonzero, its definition as a nonzero functional gives a compact smooth detecting test; symmetry permits the symmetric part. Its support must meet Z or its pairing would vanish. CLD 15.2.1(a) says every point in that support has d_K>=r. Thus a nonzero detector must meet Z at a point of d_K at least n-p-1. A closed analytic locus cannot everywhere have local dimension below this threshold.

Applying the proved removability theorem to the original canonical integration current delta_X, positive and doubly closed by n1, proves D[h]=0 whenever the analytic exceptional locus has dimension <n-1. Actual generic Artinian integration weights are retained. This does not prove that h or -h is psh or construct separately admissible U,V.

For p>=1, the interval n-p-1<=dim Z<n-1 is therefore a remaining dimensional window in this particular off-locus route: canonical nullity follows, while dimensional support alone does not prove multiplier independence. It identifies unexcluded possibilities, not an analytic counterexample. For p=0 there is no such window.

The weighted-cutoff route in n2 gives an exact direct estimate, but neither off-locus ordinary smooth zero-Hessian regularity nor vanishing weighted errors or uniformly bounded small-neighborhood cutoff masses is proved for arbitrary continuous equal-curvature pairs and arbitrary currents. Finiteness for every individual cutoff neighborhood cannot be exchanged for a uniform bound. At the critical detecting dimension, permitted tests do not manufacture a positive closed defect. No compatible current exhaustion, harmonic-test lift with ordinary-product agreement, recognition of both signs as generated psh, or ascent and faithful descent of the original current has been constructed.

The entire literal original P21.3 remains unresolved. Its residual retains every ordinary open, all complete fields including trivial valuation, good/separated/strict/boundaryless and pure n>=2 hypotheses, singularities and nilpotents, actual generic lengths, all p=0,...,n-1, and separately admissible finite continuous psh U,V with exact upstairs D[U]=D[V]. No actual analytic X,U,V,T and compact smooth alpha with nonzero detecting pairing has been exhibited. Previously removed curve, polycylinder, invariant split-toric and stated approximation ranges are not counted as new solutions. No cover is turned into a basis. Accordingly candidate=false.

The complete standalone partial paper is [P21.3-paper.tex](/workspace/research/campaigns/round-262/P21.3-entire-original-arbitrary-current/artifacts/codex-uZFDii/P21.3-paper.tex). whole-proof.md and sections/ contain complete separately bound proof bodies. native-notes.json and notes.json contain the notes. whole-source-application-ledger.json and .md record exact primary versions, literal complete immediate statements/proofs, hypotheses, applications and recursive foundations. whole-proof-coverage.json, exact-scope.json, original-scope-and-noncircularity-decision.json and decision-evidence.json expose the missing universal gates.
